headline: Humphries beats Price 6-4 in sets to win the World Grand Prix
standfirst: Luke Humphries won the double-start World Grand Prix in Leicester, beating Gerwyn Price in the final and hitting a tournament-high 29 maximums.
body: Luke Humphries won the 2026 World Grand Prix at the Mattioli Arena in Leicester, beating Gerwyn Price 6-4 in sets in the final. Price had the higher average, 95.37 to 93.16, but Humphries won the key sets in the double-start format.

Humphries did not drop a set in his first three matches, beating Dave Chisnall 2-0, Jermaine Wattimena 3-0 and Niels Zonneveld 3-0. He then beat James Wade 5-3 in the semi-finals with a 96.83 average.

Price beat Jonny Clayton 3-2 in the quarter-finals and Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in the semi-finals. Aspinall had produced the best average of the tournament, 105.15, in a 3-0 quarter-final win over Ryan Joyce.
Wade beat Gian van Veen 3-0 in the quarter-finals, averaging 96.71. Ryan Searle's 167 checkout against Van Veen in the last 16 was the highest of the week.
Humphries hit 29 maximums, ahead of Price with 27 and Aspinall with 24.
